headline: America’s Wealth Gap, Drawn to Scale
lede: One pixel stands for $5,000, but the distance between ordinary household wealth and billionaire fortunes quickly overwhelms the screen. Built from Federal Reserve data, this interactive visualization turns inequality into a physical measure—and connects the numbers to housing, healthcare, debt, and wages.

headline: Graph Theory Begins With Puzzles
lede: This openly licensed introduction treats graph theory as a practice of solving, proving, and seeing structure. Its accessible chapters make a durable mathematical subject available to self-learners and classrooms alike, though independent readers may wish for solutions to the exercises.

headline: Version Control Comes to Federal Law
lede: A date-aware reconstruction of the U.S. Code records what changed, when it changed, and which public law made the change. The system reproduces 361 of 365 tested amendments across nine titles—a practical provenance layer for lawyers, researchers, and legal AI.

headline: Genie Builds Worlds That Respond
lede: DeepMind’s Genie 4 generates interactive environments with text, imagery, simulated physics, ambient sound, and dialogue. The promise is broad—from robotics to historical reconstruction—but coherence, object permanence, and long-term control remain fragile under the glow of the demo.

headline: Ghostty 1.4 Rebuilds the Terminal Core
lede: Seven months and 2,889 commits deliver faster I/O, lower-memory scrollback, a new GTK pipeline, and complete Kitty graphics support. Ghostty also tightens its security posture and makes libghostty a more capable foundation for embedded terminal experiences.

headline: Ink Droplets Become Tiny Worlds
lede: A modified printer, an old microscope, and a carefully timed flash turn falling ink into an otherworldly landscape. Ole Bielfeldt’s winning Nikon Small World image celebrates the curious engineering behind a familiar machine—and the strange beauty hiding inside its motions.

headline: An Offline Assistant Packs the Library
lede: Survival LLM bundles local models with roughly 930,000 Wikipedia articles and a curated emergency reference collection. It can answer without the internet and index private documents, but its citations still need checking—and no model substitutes for power, tools, or practiced skills.

headline: The Apple Server Learns an Old Trick
lede: A recovered preproduction ROM reveals that Apple Network Servers could boot Mac OS while retaining their AIX identity. Through reverse-engineered drivers, firmware fixes, and carefully adapted extensions, a hidden capability returns to hardware designed to keep it concealed.

headline: Tailscale SSH Finds Its Privilege Boundary
lede: Several vulnerabilities could let an already authorized user exceed the permissions of a configured local account. Tighten SSH policies, disable forwarding where unnecessary, and update when the patched client arrives; conditional access is still access worth containing.

headline: AI Enters the Long Road to Medicine
lede: Anthropic reports early work with six biotech and pharmaceutical organizations across molecule design, genetic constructs, manufacturing, and trial planning. The bottleneck has not disappeared: promising designs still face laboratory validation, regulatory scrutiny, and human trials.
pullquote: The shortest path from a model’s design to a medicine still runs through the laboratory.
